summary: Monday sales team meeting, roughly 52 minutes, run by sales manager Chris Klevan. Structure was wins round-robin, then per-person numbers and projection reallocation for closers Andrew and Ben, then setter numbers for Kim and Kyla, then a live call review. Andrew closed three units for $7,200 cash against target and had to move $3,600 into the following two weeks; Ben closed one unit for $6,000 and moved both of his remaining units to week four. Kim logged 20 sets at a 79.6% show rate and one unit; Kyla finished with six sets. Chris coached objection handling at length — building the goal to identity level, isolating the real objection under 'will this work for me', and a full role-played word track for a prospect wanting proof. Kim and Kyla were sent to a breakout room so Kim could walk Kyla through her dialling and triage workflow. The meeting closed with a partial review of Andrew's call with Manny Nunez, cut short when Chris had to leave to take a call from his landlord.
notable: CONDUCT — after the manager left the call, closers Ben Byrne and Andrew Jin spent roughly a minute mocking two prospects for being gay, including 'Sorry, this program is not for you' and a suggestion that not working out causes it. Detailed with quotes in the flags file.

OFF-MENU OFFER — Andrew disclosed he had closed a prospect on a 'love it or leave it' rather than the standard terms, expecting the prospect to convert to the full six months after a month. Chris explicitly sanctioned it as a legitimate tool: 'love it or leave it is definitely something you can use in your back pocket for somebody who has sort of, like, trust issues... It's also just making sure that it's not the first thing you go to.' No price or term for this structure was stated.

IMPLIED REFUND — while modelling a word track for closers to use live, Chris said 'we're not going to like... Hold your money or hold you in here if you can't get the results.' This is materially different from the performance guarantee reps actually state on calls, and is being taught as a closing line.

EFFICACY COACHING — closers were instructed to assert certainty of results as biological fact and to show no doubt: 'it's science. Like, if you eat the food that we're saying to eat, and you train this way, do you really think you're not going to get good results?' and 'If they eat the foods and they do the work, the result has to happen. It's human biology has to happen' and 'don't show any sort of uncertainty in yourself. Like have full conviction that we get results.'

CRM INTEGRITY — Chris instructed that every booked call must get a custom activity in Close regardless of whether it happened, including no-shows and reschedules, and Ben effectively admitted he had not been doing it. Any close-rate denominator drawn from this CRM before 8 June is incomplete by the team's own account.

CASH VERSUS UNITS — three units produced $7,200 cash for Andrew, an average of $2,400 per unit against a $6,000 headline price, while Ben's single unit produced the full $6,000 as a PIF. Units and cash are tracked as separate lines and diverge sharply, which matters for how any revenue rollup from this corpus is read.

THIRD-PARTY LENDING IS ROUTINE — Ben on the financing provider: 'the tough thing with Paiva is it only goes up to 12 months.' Andrew was planning a follow-up call with Manny Nunez specifically to walk him through Paiva financing options.
SETTER CODES CONFIRMED — KFS is Kim Forbes-Sobers and KL is Kyla Louie, both present and named as the two setters on the team.

PRIMAL UNIVERSITY DOWNSELL IS A KNOWN HABIT — Andrew referred to rushing a prospect into Primal University as a 'mistake' he had made on an earlier call and was consciously avoiding repeating, confirming the $200/month downsell is a recurring improvisation rather than a one-off.

POSITIVE — Chris pushed back on Andrew for steering a prospect's motivation: 'Be very careful with telling somebody what their why should be.' He also refused to round Kim's 79.6% show rate up to 80: 'No, that's, that's, that's reality.'

Ben Byrne is new to this offer and openly struggling with conviction and the $6,000 price: 'that also would like help with the objection of like, well, dude, like, just not seeing the value and investing $6,000. So that's, that's been another one that's, you know, struggling with a bit.'

Chris on qualification when no gap exists: 'this is like a pretty premium transformation. These are the types of clients we work with... they're willing and able to pay thousands of dollars for it.' This is the ICP being applied as a disqualification script rather than as a booking filter.
